results.question: Why is attrition in Human Resources so much higher than in every other department?

results.sql:
SELECT department,
       ROUND(100 * AVG(CASE WHEN attrition THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 1) AS attrition_rate_pct,
       ROUND(AVG(job_satisfaction), 1) AS avg_job_satisfaction,
       ROUND(100 * AVG(CASE WHEN over_time THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 1) AS overtime_pct,
       COUNT(*) AS headcount
FROM employees
GROUP BY department
ORDER BY attrition_rate_pct DESC

results.question: Which team has the lowest job satisfaction?
results.answer: The team with the lowest job satisfaction is Research & Development / Laboratory Technician / Team 1, with an average satisfaction of 1.7 and a headcount of 6.
results.sql:
SELECT team,
       ROUND(AVG(job_satisfaction), 1) AS avg_job_satisfaction,
       COUNT(*) AS headcount
FROM employees
WHERE team IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY team
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY avg_job_satisfaction ASC
LIMIT 1

results.question: Is the difference in attrition between men and women statistically significant?
results.answer: The table shows female attrition at 14.8 % (87 of 588) and male attrition at 17.0 % (150 of 882). No statistical test results are included, so the significance of the difference cannot be determined from this data alone.
results.sql:

       COUNT(*) AS headcount,
       ROUND(100 * AVG(CASE WHEN attrition THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 1) AS attrition_rate_pct,
       SUM(CASE WHEN attrition THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS attrition_count
FROM employees
GROUP BY gender
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
